concepts.title: Work Done by a Force
concepts.body: Work is done when a force causes an object to move in the direction of the force. The amount of work depends on the magnitude of the force and the distance the object moves. For example, pushing a shopping cart across a store involves work because the force applied moves the cart forward.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
concepts.body: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion, while potential energy is the energy stored in an object due to its position or configuration. For instance, a moving car has kinetic energy, and a book placed on a shelf has potential energy due to its height above the ground.

concepts.title: Law of Conservation of Energy
concepts.body: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. For example, when a pendulum swings, its potential energy converts to kinetic energy and vice versa, but the total energy remains constant.

formulas.title: Work Done
formulas.body: W = F x s (W in joule J, F in newton N, s in meter m). This formula calculates the work done when a force F moves an object through a displacement s in the direction of the force.

formulas.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
formulas.body: Kinetic energy = (1/2) m v^2 (m in kg, v in m/s). Potential energy = m g h (m in kg, g in m/s^2, h in m). These formulas are used to calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object and the potential energy of an object due to its height.

examples.title: Everyday Example
examples.body: When you lift a bucket of water from the ground to a table, you do work against gravity. The force you apply moves the bucket upward, and the work done is stored as potential energy in the bucket.

examples.title: Applied Example
examples.body: In a hydroelectric power plant, water stored at a height has potential energy. When the water flows down, this potential energy is converted into kinetic energy, which is then used to generate electricity.

mcqs.question: What is the unit of work?
mcqs.explanation: The unit of work is joule (J). Newton (N) is the unit of force, watt (W) is the unit of power, and pascal (Pa) is the unit of pressure.

mcqs.question: A 2 kg object is moving at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula KE = (1/2) m v^2, KE = (1/2) x 2 kg x (3 m/s)^2 = 9 J. The other options are incorrect because they do not follow the correct calculation.

mcqs.question: A 5 kg object is lifted to a height of 10 m. What is its potential energy? (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula PE = m g h, PE = 5 kg x 10 m/s^2 x 10 m = 500 J. The other options are incorrect because they do not follow the correct calculation.
